items.name: Rectangle primitive (stroke + fill + opacity)
items.spec:
Add `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/rectangle.{h,cpp}` — screen-agnostic Clay helper for a flat-colored rectangle with optional stroke and optional fill opacity. API shape (final names yours; spirit of the constraints binding):

- Take ALL color/width values as REQUIRED parameters (compile-time, not opts-struct defaults) — match the precedent set by commit 63c779d. No lobby-coupled defaults.
- Knobs: fillPaletteColor (Uint8 or 'no fill' sentinel), fillOpacity (0.0–1.0 or palette-alpha-index), strokePaletteColor (Uint8 or 'no stroke'), strokeWidth (Uint8, fixed 1 px is fine for now if you want to simplify), plus sizing (caller-provided width/height OR sized-by-parent if used inside a flex container).
- The primitive emits ONE Clay element with `.backgroundColor` and `.border` configured from the params. No CUSTOM render command unless opacity-blending requires it (see C1).
- Add a render test at `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/rectangle_test.cpp` that renders 4 variants: stroke-only, fill-only, fill+stroke, fill-with-opacity-over-an-existing-color. Wired through the JSON-lines control op pattern used by other primitive tests.
- Test references at `tests/lobby-clay/rectangle_test/` (reference.png + run.sh).

NOTE: this primitive will be renamed Rectangle→Box in the next item (C0b). The historical name 'Rectangle' is preserved here as the record of what shipped first.

items.name: Rename Rectangle primitive → Box (canonical UI vocabulary)
items.spec:
Pure rename. 'Rectangle' implies a geometric shape; the canonical web/UI vocabulary for a generic styled container is 'Box' (Chakra, Mantine, NativeBase, Tamagui, Material Box). Clay itself doesn't name this concept — every CLAY({...}) is just 'an element' — so the choice is downstream. Box is shorter, role-neutral, and pairs naturally with future Row/Column/Stack siblings.

Mechanics (use `git mv` everywhere to preserve history):

1. `git mv clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/rectangle.h clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/box.h`
2. `git mv clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/rectangle.cpp clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/box.cpp`
3. `git mv clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/rectangle_test.cpp clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/box_test.cpp`
4. `git mv tests/lobby-clay/rectangle_test tests/lobby-clay/box_test`

Inside the moved files:

5. Header guard: `SILENCER_UI_CLAY_PRIMITIVES_RECTANGLE_H` → `SILENCER_UI_CLAY_PRIMITIVES_BOX_H` in box.h.
6. Function rename: `silencer::ui::primitives::Rectangle(...)` → `Box(...)` everywhere (header, impl, test, any caller — there shouldn't be any non-test callers yet because C3+ haven't run).
7. `#include "rectangle.h"` → `#include "box.h"` in box.cpp and box_test.cpp.
8. Docstring rewrites in box.h: every mention of 'rectangle' → 'box'. The word 'rectangle' can stay where it refers to the GEOMETRIC primitive being drawn (e.g., 'emits a rectangle on screen') vs. the primitive's NAME.
9. In `clients/silencer/src/net/controldispatch.cpp`: rename the control op `clay_rectangle_test` → `clay_box_test`.
10. In `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/clay_bridge.h`: rename the forward decl `RunRectangleTest` → `RunBoxTest`.
11. In `tests/lobby-clay/box_test/run.sh`: update the `cli` invocation from `clay_rectangle_test` to `clay_box_test`.
12. Refresh CMake source list because renamed files don't auto-pick-up: `cmake -B build -S clients/silencer`.
13. Build + run the test. Pixdiff MUST still be 0.0000% — this is a pure rename, no visual change. If pixdiff changes, a string slipped through; find it.

Nothing else changes — same API shape, same params, same rendered pixels. The `passes` flag for C0 stays true; this iteration's commit just renames artifacts.

items.name: Box stroke halos (multi-tone outer + inner rings)
items.spec:
The bright stroke in the lobby BG sprite is technically a 1-px palette idx 216 line — Clay's default border reproduces those pixels exactly — BUT the visual depth around it comes from the BG sprite's decorative dithered framing (palette idx 75 / 81 / 211 in 1–2 px bands on either side). Once C7 drops the BG sprite, those framing pixels vanish and the bare 1-px stroke looks naked against flat black. To recreate the legacy chrome depth without baking back any texture, extend the Box primitive with multi-tone halos: bands of color around the primary stroke that the bridge renders procedurally.

API additions to `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/box.{h,cpp}` (post-C0b rename):

- `strokeOuterHaloColor: Uint8` (0 = no outer halo)
- `strokeOuterHaloWidth: Uint8` (px count, 0–2)
- `strokeInnerHaloColor: Uint8` (0 = no inner halo)
- `strokeInnerHaloWidth: Uint8` (px count, 0–2)

All four are REQUIRED parameters — match 63c779d precedent. The four-zero case (no halos) MUST fall through to the existing Clay `.border` path (cheap; no new render commands).

When ANY halo is non-zero, the bridge routes through a new `CustomKind::BoxStroke` (or similar — name yours) that renders the stroke as concentric inset rectangles: outermost first (at the box's outer edge), then progressively inward, ending with the primary stroke. Inner halos extend further inward from the primary. Each ring is 1 px wide repeated `<thing>HaloWidth` times.

Use the inspection helper at `/tmp/inspect_lobby_stroke.py` (already on disk) to sample the actual chrome halo colors at multiple corners of the lobby BG. The bright primary is consistently idx 216; the outer halo around it is approximately idx 75 (rgb 8,40,8) one ring out, and idx 211 (rgb 0,32,0) at two rings out. The inner halo is approximately idx 81. Sample at 3–4 different lobby rectangle edges to confirm consistency before committing the canonical values.

Document the canonical values in `docs/plans/lobby-chrome-rectangles.md` (the doc C2 will create) so each panel item (C3–C7) passes the same halo params. Suggested default for the lobby's chrome rectangles: `strokeColor=216, strokeOuterHaloColor=75, strokeOuterHaloWidth=1, strokeInnerHaloColor=81, strokeInnerHaloWidth=1`. The agent on C2 fine-tunes after sampling.

Update the box_test scene to add a 5th variant: box with halos on (visible against the test scene's existing backgrounds). Add a sixth panel-style test scene: a Box rendered with the lobby's canonical halo params against a flat black background — this is the visual the user will review when C0c lands.

Screenshot DM'd. No lobby includes in box.{h,cpp}.

items.name: Bridge: alpha-blended Box fills via palette alphaed LUT
items.spec:
The current Clay bridge dispatches RECTANGLE by writing a single palette index per pixel — no alpha. For the Box primitive's `fillOpacity`, the bridge must route to the renderer's existing palette-blend path. Read `clients/silencer/src/render/palette.cpp` (look for `alphaed`) to understand the LUT: `alphaed[palette][src*256 + dst]` returns the blended palette index. Each Box pixel at opacity α maps to `alphaed[…][srcColor*256 + dstColor]` with α as the LUT bank selector (or, simpler first cut: pick one alpha level for now, e.g. 50%, and document that opacity is currently quantized to that single level — full N-level alpha can come later if needed).

Extend the bridge in `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/clay_bridge.cpp`. If the simplest path is a new CustomKind (e.g. `CustomKind::FillBlend`) that the Box primitive routes through when `fillOpacity < 1.0`, that's fine — but prefer just enhancing the existing RECTANGLE dispatch to read the userData for an optional opacity hint.

Add a smoke test: a fully-opaque red box underneath a 50%-opaque blue box should produce a known mid-tone palette index in the overlap region. Pixdiff against a hand-crafted reference < 0.5%.

items.spec:

The existing TitleBar chrome elements (title text 'Silencer', version 'v.X', map-name overlay, Go Back BankButton) currently live as four separate `floating @ROOT (x, y)` elements in `clients/silencer/src/ui/screens/lobby_clay/lobby_clay_screen.cpp` (search `LobbyTitle`, `LobbyVer`, `LobbyMapName`, `LobbyGoBackWrap`). Relocate them INSIDE the new title bar Box using flex layout — `LEFT_TO_RIGHT`, gaps, alignment. Don't keep `floating @ROOT` for title-bar elements after this iteration.

The LobbyBg sprite STAYS emitted underneath in this iteration (so misalignment between your new Boxes and the baked chrome is visible). Don't drop it yet — that's C7.

Picking exact pixel coords: aim to match the baked rectangle positions to within ~2 px on each edge so the chrome looks coherent during the transition. The Box stroke color comes from C2's documented sample.
